description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the #1917 review probe (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/s491a/p1917-idioms.pl row 7, p-hires.pl, p-hires2.pl); PRE-EXISTING on main 9e323b30 and unchanged by s491a except for the message text.

  use Time::HiRes qw(time);  my $t = time;  print "frac=", ($t =~ /\./ ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl: frac=1        PCL: the program DIES at the `use` (whole-program failure, loud).
The same for `require Time::HiRes` and the string-eval spelling.  Storable and Digest::MD5 fail the same way on this box (pclxs is PARKED since s485, so nothing XS loads) -- they are #1607's "XS THROUGH PCLXS" list and NOT this task; Time::HiRes is different because its useful surface is five functions that need NO XS bridge at all.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the README's own speed claims invite people to time things, and `use Time::HiRes qw(time)` is line one of most scripts that do.  A first-hour alpha user hits this.

DESIGN QUESTION FOR FABLE (rule 9a decides the layer): Time::HiRes is CORE perl, not CPAN, so it may live in the runtime -- but the smallest correct shape is a plain-Perl shim `lib/Time/HiRes.pm` (exports, prototypes, `tv_interval` arithmetic, `usleep`/`nanosleep` in terms of `sleep`) over ONE or TWO runtime primitives reached through the blessed shim-dispatch seam (`builtin::`-style, DECIDED s377): a float `time` (sb-ext:get-time-of-day or sb-unix:unix-gettimeofday -> seconds + microseconds) and a fractional `sleep` (CL `sleep` takes a real).  Surface to cover, probed vs perl: `time`, `sleep` (returns the slept seconds), `usleep`, `nanosleep`, `gettimeofday` (list AND scalar context), `tv_interval([..],[..])` and with one argument, `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` + the CLOCK_* constants, `clock_getres`; `alarm`/`ualarm`/`setitimer` are signal-driven -> out of scope, named in not-supported.md if left.  `use Time::HiRes qw(time)` must OVERRIDE the builtin `time` in the importing package only (perl's import of a sub named like a builtin) -- probe that PCL's bareword `time` honours an imported sub of that name (#266's callable classifier) before writing the shim.

PORTABILITY (USER 2026-09-06, "not software for our laptop"): gettimeofday through sb-unix is Linux/macOS-fine; the install matrix + a macOS leg must stay green.

BAR: lib/ shim + a small cl/ primitive -> full sweep, the companion files that `use Time::HiRes` (grep -a the suite: lib/Time-HiRes is not in the population, but op/time.t, op/sleep.t, op/alarm.t and many io/ files import it -- expect UPWARD movers, each spliced with this task as cause), `tools/ir-inventory.pl` if an export is added, guard `Pl/t/time-hires-01.t` (values asserted as RANGES, never exact times), docs/shipped-modules.md corrected (it promises a file that does not exist), README/STATUS mention.

=== USER REQUEST + EASE ASSESSMENT (s491, Fable, 2026-09-19) ===
USER, on reading this finding: "If the Time::HiRes can be done easily, please put a shim on the todo."  ON THE TODO: this task; a candidate for the next correctness batch.

HOW EASY, MEASURED: the PRIMITIVES are trivial -- the runtime already has `p-time` and `p-sleep` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~19595-19633); `p-sleep` TRUNCATES its argument to whole seconds (`(truncate (to-number secs))`), so a fractional `sleep` is one line, and a float `time` is sb-ext:get-time-of-day (or sb-unix:unix-gettimeofday) seconds + microseconds/1e6.  The shim's Perl side (exports, `tv_interval`, `usleep`/`nanosleep` in terms of the fractional sleep, `gettimeofday` in both contexts) is an hour.

THE REAL SIZE IS ONE GENERIC MECHANISM, probed (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/s491a/p-import-builtin-name.pl): **an imported sub named like a builtin does NOT override the builtin in PCL.**  A package whose `import` installs `*{caller."::time"}` and `*{caller."::sleep"}`: perl then calls the imported subs for a bare `time` / `sleep(0.25)` (t=12345.5, s=slept:0.25); PCL calls the builtins (t=<epoch>, s=0).  `use Time::HiRes qw(time sleep)` depends on exactly that.  perl's rule: a sub IMPORTED into the package (not merely defined there) overrides an OVERRIDABLE builtin (those with a prototype -- `time`, `sleep`, `open`, `die`, ... -- not `print`/`sort`/...) for barewords compiled after the import.  In PCL this is a PARSE fact available at compile time: the `use` line's import list is already read for prototypes (`_merge_module_prototypes`), so "the names this `use` imports" is known; what is missing is the builtin-name lookup consulting it (#266's callable classifier is the place -- ONE predicate, keyed on the mechanism, never on Time::HiRes).  Related open work: op/override.t (#1870, `CORE::GLOBAL::`) is the sibling spelling of the same perl rule.

SO: easy = yes for the module; the mechanism is a small, well-bounded compiler task that also pays for every other module that exports a builtin's name (`Time::HiRes`, `POSIX qw(sleep)`-style imports, `autodie`'s wrappers, test mocks).  Order: (1) the generic override, with its own guard (a fixture module, no real module name in Pl/ or cl/), (2) the fractional p-sleep + the float-time primitive, (3) lib/Time/HiRes.pm, (4) docs/shipped-modules.md corrected.


=== STEP 1 IS TASK #1870 -- ONE MECHANISM, TWO SPELLINGS (s491, Fable, after the USER asked "so the overloading of builtins will work? that isn't tested?") ===
It IS tested: perl's own t/op/override.t is exactly this, PCL runs 3 ok / 17 not ok of its 36 rows (16 never produced), and the census (s473t6b) attributes the WHOLE file to #1870: "builtin OVERRIDE via *CORE::GLOBAL::NAME or *main::NAME is not honoured -- PCL emits the builtin's own call form".  It is a known, recorded, unfixed bug; PCL's own Pl/t gate does not show it because the gate guards what works.
MEASURED per spelling (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/s491a/p-override-spellings.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main 4da6482b):
  (a) `use subs qw(time); sub time {...}`                 perl: the sub      PCL: the sub      RIGHT already
  (b) a sub IMPORTED by glob assignment at BEGIN (Exporter -- the Time::HiRes spelling)   perl: the sub   PCL: the BUILTIN   WRONG
  (c) `BEGIN { *CORE::GLOBAL::hex = sub {...} }`            perl: the sub      PCL: the BUILTIN   WRONG  (#1870's spelling)
  (d) a sub merely DEFINED in the package, no import        perl: the BUILTIN  PCL: the BUILTIN   RIGHT (do not break it)
  (e) `CORE::sleep(...)`                                    always the builtin on both            RIGHT
So (a) proves the emitter CAN route a builtin's name to a user sub -- find how `use subs` does it (grep Pl/ for `subs`) and route (b) and (c) through the SAME path (CLAUDE.md rule 11); do NOT build a second mechanism.  perl's rule, for the record: a builtin is overridden for a package when a sub of that name was IMPORTED into it (the glob's IMPORTED_CV flag: assigned from another package at compile time), or for every package via CORE::GLOBAL::; only OVERRIDABLE builtins qualify (the ones `prototype("CORE::name")` answers for -- not print/sort/map/...).
ACCEPTANCE for step 1 = op/override.t's rows (expect a large upward move; splice row by row with #1870 + this task as cause) + the five-spelling probe identical to perl.  Close #1870 with it.

=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
Step 1 (the generic override) is #1870, done in the same session.  Then:

`lib/Time/HiRes.pm`, plain Perl, over FOUR primitives on the blessed
`builtin::` seam -- `hires_time` (epoch seconds as a double, via
sb-ext:get-time-of-day), `hires_sleep` (a fractional sleep that answers the
seconds actually slept), `hires_clock` and `hires_clock_res`.  Everything else
the module offers below its signal-driven timers is arithmetic over those and
is written in the shim: time, sleep, usleep, nanosleep, gettimeofday (LIST and
SCALAR), tv_interval (one and two arguments), clock_gettime, clock_getres,
CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC, stat, utime and the d_* capability flags.

`stat`/`utime` are there because core File::Copy line 19 imports them by name
(`BEGIN { eval q{ use Time::HiRes qw( stat utime ) } }`); they delegate to
CORE's.

CORE::sleep still TRUNCATES (`sleep 0.25` sleeps 0), as perl does -- the
fractional sleep is the module's, not the builtin's.

Probe hires1.pl: 15 rows byte-identical to perl 5.40.3, including that the
imported `time` displaces the builtin in the importing package only.  Guard
Pl/t/time-hires-01.t (12 rows, values asserted as RANGES), inverse-verified on
a 5ce155cb extraction where 11 fail.  ualarm/setitimer/getitimer/
clock_nanosleep/clock() are named in docs/not-supported.md with the reason
(PCL installs a Unix handler for SIGALRM only).  docs/shipped-modules.md
corrected: it promised a `cl/modules/time-hires.lisp` that never existed, and
now carries the shim-plus-seam pattern as the one to copy.

PORTABILITY: sb-ext:get-time-of-day is SBCL's portable gettimeofday (Linux and
macOS both answer it) and the monotonic clock is CL's own
get-internal-real-time -- no sb-unix or sb-posix symbol is named.  The CLOCK_*
ids are PCL's own consistent pair (Linux's numbers) and are never handed to
the OS; docs/not-supported.md says so.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 1 (0684b77e).  lib/Time/HiRes.pm is plain Perl over four
primitives on the blessed `builtin::` seam (hires_time, hires_sleep,
hires_clock, hires_clock_res): time / sleep / usleep / nanosleep /
gettimeofday (both contexts) / tv_interval / clock_gettime / clock_getres /
stat / utime, byte-identical to perl on a 15-row probe.  ualarm / setitimer /
getitimer are named in docs/not-supported.md.  docs/shipped-modules.md
CORRECTED: the `cl/modules/time-hires.lisp` it promised never existed, and the
lesson is in the doc -- "needs the host" was one clock and one sleep.
